---
title: "Error budgets under estimated pairwise probabilities"
subtitle: "4.14 · after the postrank theory book, ch. 21"
description: "How a bound on Monte Carlo error changes which reports can satisfy an error budget."
---

A report meeting an error budget under estimated pair probabilities can fail under the exact posterior. A uniform error margin ε brackets exact feasibility between inner and outer sets.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Estimated pass.** For A above B, estimated share .200 passes budget .25 while exact share .300 fails, bracketed by .15 and .35.
- **Negative inner.** At estimated share 0, signed inner threshold −.05 stays negative so A above B is excluded.
- **Exactly two.** Requiring two grades excludes full withholding and leaves 0 reports in the inner set.
- **Radius too small.** Margin .05 breaks the error bound ("no") and admits an inner report that fails the exact budget.
- **Raw comparisons.** Removing float tolerance makes the strict bound check read "no" on tiny floating-point excess.
- **Fixed-S IID.** With 1,000 draws across six sites, score B has weight 0 yet stays protected by its .03 budget.

<details>
<summary>Model notes</summary>

The two-unit example specifies exact and estimated pairwise probabilities directly. In the fixed-sample simulation, all estimated pair coefficients fall within the uniform error margin with probability at least $1 - \alpha$ across repeated draws of the same size from the supplied law. Compliance under the model is determined by the exact expected wrong share, and signed thresholds can be negative or exceed one.

</details>
